subtype: Approach: freezing because the plan was never practised [Pitfall]
passage: The smoke alarm shrieked at 2 a.m. Pradeep sat up. He knew there was a plan; Amma had read it out once in the living room, but he had never walked it. Now he stood frozen in his doorway with tears running down his face. The words swirled: stairs, low, door... which first? "Pradeep!" His mother Preeti rushed in, took his hand and said, "Low. Follow me." They went down the stairs together and out to the gate, where neighbours were already gathering. Pradeep shivered and sobbed. Afterwards he asked whether they could really walk the way out, tomorrow, all of it.

qa.q: What time did the smoke alarm go off?
qa.a: The smoke alarm shrieked at 2 a.m.

qa.q: What was Pradeep feeling as he stood in the doorway?
qa.a: Terrified and confused, so frozen that he cried, because the plan words swirled in his head.

qa.q: What could the family do now, and why?
qa.a: They could walk the escape route together, by day and once in the dark, so the steps become movements and not only words.

qa.q: How might Preeti have felt when she found Pradeep standing there?
qa.a: Preeti was probably alarmed and protective, since she rushed in and took his hand straight away.

grounding: A child who only heard about an escape plan freezes at a real smoke alarm and needs a parent to lead him out.
